p: Glossary
x: A small, cheap chip made by Espressif that contains a tiny computer (a microcontroller) plus Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. Think of it as the brain of a smart gadget: a smart air conditioner, a video doorbell, a digital scale.

p: Glossary
x: A very small computer on a single chip that does one job over and over, like the brain of a washing machine. It has no operating system: its program starts running the moment it powers up.

p: Glossary
x: Another name for a microcontroller: a tiny single-chip computer built to control devices.

p: Glossary
x: A whole system on one chip: processor, memory, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and inputs/outputs all packed inside a single chip. The ESP32 is an SoC.

p: Glossary
x: An all-purpose input/output pin. You can tell it to put out a voltage (for example, to light an LED) or to read a voltage (for example, to see whether a button is pressed).

p: Glossary
x: A metal leg on the board that you connect a wire to. Each pin has a number and a job.

p: Glossary
x: Turns a smoothly varying voltage (say 1.6 V) into a number (0 to 4095 on the ESP32). It is like a ruler that turns a length into a number.

p: Glossary
x: The opposite of an ADC: it turns a number (0 to 255) into a real voltage between 0 and 3.3 V. The classic ESP32 has two DAC outputs, on GPIO25 and GPIO26.

p: Glossary
x: Switching a pin on and off very fast. If it is on 25% of the time, an LED shines at about a quarter of its brightness. It is like quickly opening and closing a tap to reduce the water flow.

p: Glossary
x: The percentage of time a PWM signal is on. 0% means always off, 100% means always on, and 50% means on half the time.

p: Glossary
x: The ESP32 hardware block that generates PWM signals. Despite its name, it is also used for motors and servos.

p: Glossary
x: The speed of serial data, in bits per second. Both sides must use the same number (for example 115200), or you will see garbled, meaningless characters.

p: Glossary
x: A window in the Arduino IDE that shows the messages the ESP32 sends with Serial.print. It is the best tool for finding out what your program is actually doing.

p: Glossary
x: Simple serial communication over two wires: TX (transmit) and RX (receive). The TX of one side connects to the RX of the other, like one person's mouth talking to the other's ear.

p: Glossary
x: The sending pin in a serial connection.

p: Glossary
x: The receiving pin in a serial connection.

p: Glossary
x: A protocol that connects many devices over just two wires (SDA for data, SCL for the clock). Each device has its own address, like house numbers on one street.

p: Glossary
x: The data wire in I2C. On the ESP32 it is GPIO21 by default.

p: Glossary
x: The clock wire in I2C; it sets the rhythm of the transfer. On the ESP32 it is GPIO22 by default.

p: Glossary
x: A fast protocol with four wires (MOSI, MISO, SCK, CS), used for SD cards and fast displays. Each device gets its own CS wire.

p: Glossary
x: In SPI, the data wire that carries data from the ESP32 to the device.

p: Glossary
x: In SPI, the data wire that carries data from the device back to the ESP32.

p: Glossary
x: The clock wire in SPI.

p: Glossary
x: The device-select wire in SPI. When it goes LOW, it means "I'm talking to you now."

p: Glossary
x: A resistor that pulls a pin up to 3.3 V (HIGH) when nothing else is driving it, so its value doesn't float around randomly. The ESP32 has built-in pull-ups: INPUT_PULLUP.

p: Glossary
x: A resistor that pulls a pin down to ground (LOW) when nothing else is driving it.

p: Glossary
x: A pin that isn't connected to anything. Like an antenna, it picks up noise and its value jumps up and down. The fix: a pull-up or pull-down resistor.

p: Glossary
x: The "1" or on state; on the ESP32 that means about 3.3 V.

p: Glossary
x: The "0" or off state; that means 0 V (ground).

p: Glossary
x: The 0 V reference point of a circuit. All parts of a circuit must share a common GND, otherwise their voltages mean nothing.

p: Glossary
x: The 3.3 V power pin. The ESP32 runs on 3.3 V, and its pins cannot tolerate 5 V.

p: Glossary
x: The board's voltage input (usually 5 V from USB). On some boards it is labeled 5V.

p: Glossary
x: Electrical pressure, like the water pressure in a pipe. Measured in volts.

p: Glossary
x: How much electricity flows past a point each second, like how much water flows through a pipe. Measured in amperes (amps) or milliamps (mA).

p: Glossary
x: Opposition to the flow of current, like squeezing a water pipe narrower. Measured in ohms. Ohm's law: V = I × R.

p: Glossary
x: A diode that gives off light. It has a long leg (anode, +) and a short leg (cathode, −), and must always be wired with a series resistor so it doesn't burn out.

p: Glossary
x: A board full of holes for building circuits without soldering. Each short row of five holes is connected together underneath.

p: Glossary
x: The wireless local network the ESP32 uses to connect to your home router and the internet. The ESP32 only supports the 2.4 GHz band.

p: Glossary
x: The name of a Wi-Fi network: the same name you see in your phone's list of Wi-Fi networks.

p: Glossary
x: A device's address on a network, such as 192.168.1.50. It is like a house number for internet packets.

p: Glossary
x: The strength of the received Wi-Fi signal, in dBm. It is a negative number: -50 is excellent, -70 is okay, -85 is weak.

p: Glossary
x: The language a browser and a web server use to talk. The browser sends a request, and the server sends back a response.

p: Glossary
x: A program that answers requests from a browser. The ESP32 can itself act as a small web server.

p: Glossary
x: Classic Bluetooth, used for continuous data streams such as audio or a wireless serial terminal. Only the classic ESP32 has it; the C3 and S3 do not.

p: Glossary
x: Low-power Bluetooth, for small messages and very low battery drain. Data is organized into services and characteristics.

p: Glossary
x: A unique 128-bit ID. In BLE, every service and characteristic is named by one.

p: Glossary
x: A lightweight messaging protocol for the Internet of Things. Devices connect to a broker and publish or subscribe to messages on topics, a bit like channels in a chat app.

p: Glossary
x: The central MQTT server. It takes messages from senders and delivers them to everyone subscribed to that topic, like a post office.

p: Glossary
x: The address of a message in MQTT, such as home/livingroom/temp. The + and # wildcards let you pick several topics at once.

p: Glossary
x: How sure MQTT is that a message arrives: 0 means "send once and forget", 1 means "arrive at least once", 2 means "arrive exactly once".

p: Glossary
x: Espressif's own protocol for sending messages directly between ESP32 boards without a router. It is very fast and uses little power. Version 1 allows up to 250 bytes per message; version 2 (in newer cores) allows up to 1470 bytes.

t: MAC Address — Media Access Control Address
p: Glossary
x: A device's unique network serial number, such as 24:6F:28:AA:BB:CC. In ESP-NOW you use it to choose which board receives a message.

p: Glossary
x: Extra RAM outside the main chip (usually 4 or 8 MB). The ESP32-CAM needs it to hold large photos.

p: Glossary
x: The memory where your program and files are stored. It keeps its contents when the power is off, like a computer's hard drive.

p: Glossary
x: Fast working memory that holds your variables while the program runs; it is wiped when the power goes off. The ESP32 has about 520 KB.

p: Glossary
x: Almost the whole ESP32 shuts down and current drops to about 10 µA. When it wakes up, the program starts over from the beginning (setup).

p: Glossary
x: The processor pauses but memory is kept, so the program continues from the very next line when it wakes. Current draw is about 0.8 mA.

p: Glossary
x: An ultra-low-power part of the ESP32 that stays awake during deep sleep. It includes a timer, a few pins (RTC GPIOs) and 8 KB of RTC memory.

p: Glossary
x: What wakes the chip from sleep: a timer, a button (ext0/ext1), touch, and, in light sleep, UART or GPIO.

p: Glossary
x: Touch-sensitive pins: the classic ESP32 has 10 of them. Touching one with your finger changes its capacitance, so it returns a different number. No physical button needed.

p: Glossary
x: A pin that matters at power-up. At the moment the ESP32 turns on, it reads the voltage on these pins (GPIO0, 2, 5, 12, 15) to decide how to boot. Wiring them wrongly can stop the board from booting.

p: Glossary
x: The BOOT button on the board is wired to GPIO0. Holding it down while resetting puts the ESP32 into the mode where it accepts a new program.

p: Glossary
x: The EN button is the board's reset button. Pressing it restarts the program from the beginning.

p: Glossary
x: The program written into a microcontroller's flash memory, which runs as soon as the device powers up.

p: Glossary
x: Sending the compiled program from your computer to the ESP32 over the USB cable.

p: Glossary
x: Translating the C++ code you wrote into machine code the ESP32 understands. Typos and syntax errors are caught at this stage.

p: Glossary
x: Ready-made code someone already wrote to make working with a part or protocol easier, like a tried-and-tested recipe.

p: Glossary
x: Software that teaches Windows how to talk to the board's USB chip (CP2102 or CH340). Without it, the COM port won't show up.

p: Glossary
x: The port your computer uses to talk to the board: COM3 on Windows, /dev/ttyUSB0 on Linux, and /dev/cu.usbserial on a Mac.

p: Glossary
x: A USB-to-serial converter chip found on many ESP32 boards. Its driver is installed from the Silicon Labs website.

p: Glossary
x: A cheap USB-to-serial converter chip found on many Chinese-made boards. It needs its own driver.

p: Glossary
x: A function that runs only once, right after power-up or reset. This is where initial settings go.

p: Glossary
x: A function that runs over and over forever after setup. It is the heart of the program.

p: Glossary
x: Freezes the program completely for a number of milliseconds. It is simple, but nothing else can happen during that time.

p: Glossary
x: Returns how many milliseconds have passed since the board powered up. Used for timing without freezing the program (no delay).

p: Glossary
x: When you press a button, its metal contacts bounce for a few milliseconds, so the ESP32 sees several presses. Debouncing means ignoring that bounce.

p: Glossary
x: The hardware instantly pauses the main program to run a short function (an ISR). It is like a doorbell that interrupts whatever you are doing.

p: Glossary
x: A motor that moves to a specific angle (0 to 180 degrees) instead of spinning continuously. It is controlled with pulses 0.5 to 2.5 ms long at 50 Hz.

p: Glossary
x: A light-sensitive resistor: its resistance is low in bright light and high in the dark. Paired with a fixed resistor it forms a voltage divider, so the ESP32 can read the light level.

p: Glossary
x: A variable resistor (a knob) with three legs. Turning it changes the voltage on the middle leg anywhere between 0 and 3.3 V.

p: Glossary
x: Two resistors in series between a voltage and ground. The voltage at the middle point is split according to their ratio: Vout = Vin × R2 / (R1 + R2).

p: Glossary
x: A cheap temperature and humidity sensor with a single data wire. Temperature accuracy is ±0.5 °C. It needs at least 2 seconds between readings.

p: Glossary
x: A small 0.96-inch display with 128×64 pixels, where each pixel makes its own light. It uses the SSD1306 chip and talks over I2C.

p: Glossary
x: The controller chip in the most common small OLED displays. Its I2C address is usually 0x3C.

p: Glossary
x: The satellite positioning system. The NEO-6M module sends coordinates as NMEA text sentences over UART.

p: Glossary
x: The text format GPS modules output: sentences like $GPGGA,... that the TinyGPS++ library parses for you.

p: Glossary
x: A memory card for storing files. It connects over SPI (or SD_MMC on the ESP32-CAM) and must be formatted as FAT32.

p: Glossary
x: A small operating system running inside the ESP32 that lets several tasks run at the same time. Even Arduino's loop() is itself a task.

p: Glossary
x: An independent thread of execution in FreeRTOS with its own loop, like several cooks working at the same time in one kitchen.

p: Glossary
x: Two processor cores: the classic ESP32 has two Xtensa cores. Wi-Fi usually runs on core 0 and your program on core 1.

p: Glossary
x: A simple text format for structured data, such as {"temp": 24.5}. It is very common in IoT for sending data between devices.

p: Glossary
x: The interface a service offers for programs to use, like a restaurant menu that tells you what you can order.

p: Glossary
x: Everyday objects (lamps, air conditioners, plant pots) that are connected to the internet and send data or take commands.

p: Glossary
x: A free online simulator that runs the ESP32 and other parts in your browser, even with virtual Wi-Fi. Practice without buying any hardware.

p: Glossary
x: A professional VS Code extension for programming microcontrollers. It manages libraries and projects much more cleanly than the Arduino IDE.

p: Glossary
x: A simple, free program for writing and uploading code to Arduino and ESP32 boards. The best place to start.

p: Glossary
x: The part of the Arduino IDE that installs support packages for new boards (such as esp32 by Espressif).

p: Glossary
x: The text you give an AI. The more precise it is (board, pins, library, error message), the better the answer you get.

p: Glossary
x: A low-voltage guard: if the supply voltage suddenly sags (for example, a poor USB cable when Wi-Fi switches on), the ESP32 resets itself and you see the message "Brownout detector was triggered".

p: Glossary
x: A service in your router that automatically gives every device that connects an IP address, like a hotel receptionist handing each guest a room number.

p: Glossary
x: A protocol for getting the exact time from internet servers. The ESP32 has no battery-backed clock, so after every power-up it gets the time from NTP.

p: Glossary
x: Lets you find a device on your home network by a name like esp32.local instead of an IP number.

p: Glossary
x: How data is organized in BLE: a device has several services, and each service has several characteristics, like the shelves and drawers of a cabinet.

p: Glossary
x: A single value in BLE (for example, the temperature) with its own UUID and permissions to read, write or notify.

p: Glossary
x: The ESP32 automatically pushes a fresh value to a subscribed phone, so the phone doesn't have to keep asking.

p: Glossary
x: Short messages a BLE device broadcasts over and over so phones can find it when they scan.

p: Glossary
x: A Classic Bluetooth profile that works like a wireless serial cable. iPhones do not support it.

p: Glossary
x: An electromechanical switch: a small signal from the ESP32 turns another circuit (a lamp, say) on and off.

p: Glossary
x: An input that is activated by LOW (0 V) rather than HIGH. Most cheap relay modules work this way.

p: Glossary
x: A router setting that forwards requests from the internet to a device inside your home. Risky for beginners.

p: Glossary
x: A C++ string written as R"tag(...)tag", in which you don't need to escape quotes or new lines. Great for putting HTML inside your code.

p: Glossary
x: A JavaScript function in the browser that gets data from a server (for example, the ESP32) without reloading the page.

p: Glossary
x: A bit an I2C device sends after each byte, meaning "got it". If it doesn't come back after the address (a NACK), there is no device at that address.

p: Glossary
x: An output that can only pull the wire down to ground; to go HIGH it needs a pull-up resistor. The I2C wires work this way.

p: Glossary
x: Using two separate thresholds for switching on and off (for example, on above 2600 and off below 2200) so small noise doesn't make the output flicker on and off.

p: Glossary
x: Weakening the ADC input so it can read a wider voltage range (up to about 3.1 V). The ESP32 default is the strongest attenuation (11dB).

p: Glossary
x: A short function that runs immediately when an interrupt happens. It must be very short: no delay, no Serial.print.

p: Glossary
x: Tells the compiler that this variable may change outside the normal flow of the program (for example, inside an ISR), so it must read it from memory every time.

p: Glossary
x: Places a function in fast internal RAM, so the interrupt can run without crashing even while the flash memory is busy.

p: Glossary
x: A number the GPS gives for the quality of the horizontal position: below 2 is excellent, above 5 is poor.

p: Glossary
x: The first time a GPS powers up with no saved satellite data. Getting a position fix can take several minutes, even under open sky.

p: Glossary
x: A text file where each line is a table row and the columns are separated by commas. Excel opens it directly.

p: Glossary
x: The memory-card file system that the ESP32 SD library understands. Cards larger than 32 GB usually come formatted as exFAT and must be reformatted.

p: Glossary
x: When an AI confidently makes up something false or nonexistent, such as a function that isn't in the library or a pin that isn't on the board.

p: Glossary
x: A cap on how many messages can be sent in a period of time (for example, at most one alert every 10 minutes), so your phone or the server doesn't get flooded with repeats.

p: Glossary
x: A "last will" message a device leaves with the broker when it connects. If the device drops off suddenly, the broker publishes it on its behalf (for example, "offline").

p: Glossary
x: A message whose latest copy the broker keeps, so any new subscriber immediately gets the most recent value.

p: Glossary
x: The current a regulator itself uses with no load, even while the ESP32 sleeps. For a battery-powered device it should be just a few microamps.

p: Glossary
x: A linear regulator that keeps working even when the input voltage is only slightly above the output (for example, a 3.7 V battery down to 3.3 V).

p: Glossary
x: Before you build, you write down exactly what the device must do and how it will be tested.

p: Glossary
x: A device saved in the ESP-NOW "address book" that you can send messages to.

p: Glossary
x: A function you write but never call yourself; the library calls it whenever something happens (for example, a message arrives). Like leaving your phone number with a courier.

p: Glossary
x: A named bundle of several variables, like a printed form with a few boxes (temperature, humidity, message number) that gets sent all at once.

p: Glossary
x: Empty bytes the compiler inserts inside a struct to keep data aligned. That is why sizeof is sometimes larger than the sum of the member sizes.

p: Glossary
x: The 2-megapixel camera sensor on the ESP32-CAM, which compresses images to JPEG by itself.

p: Glossary
x: The area of RAM that holds one complete image. On the ESP32-CAM it usually lives in PSRAM.

p: Glossary
x: The fast hardware SD card interface, in 1-bit or 4-bit mode. The ESP32-CAM uses it instead of SPI.

p: Glossary
x: Taking photos at a fixed interval (for example, every 5 minutes) and turning them into a sped-up video, like watching a flower open in a few seconds.

p: Glossary
x: A label that puts a variable in RTC memory so it survives deep sleep. It is still reset to zero if power is cut completely.

p: Glossary
x: A library that stores key-value pairs in flash memory, so they survive even a power cut. The modern replacement for EEPROM.

p: Glossary
x: The multimeter beeps when the resistance between two points is very low, showing they are connected. Only use it on a circuit with the power off.

p: Glossary
x: A dull, blobby solder joint that hasn't properly bonded to the pad, so the connection cuts in and out.

p: Glossary
x: Excess solder that joins two neighboring pins and short-circuits them.

p: Glossary
x: A substance that cleans oxide off metal surfaces so solder flows easily and forms a shiny joint.

p: Glossary
x: A strip of metal pins soldered onto a module so it can plug into a breadboard.

p: Glossary
x: A ready-made wire with male or female ends for connecting parts on a breadboard.

p: Glossary
x: A module (usually built with BSS138 transistors) that converts signals between 3.3 V and 5 V in both directions.

p: Glossary
x: A 100 nF capacitor placed close to a chip's power pin to soak up fast voltage noise.

p: Glossary
x: The 12 standard resistor values in each decade: 10, 12, 15, 18, 22, 27, 33, 39, 47, 56, 68, 82 (and the same numbers times powers of 10).

p: Glossary
x: The lowest voltage a digital input reliably reads as "1" (HIGH). For the ESP32 it is about 0.75 times the supply voltage.

p: Glossary
x: How far a part's real value may be from its marked value, in percent. For example, a 10 kΩ resistor with 5% tolerance is somewhere between 9.5 and 10.5 kΩ.

t: USB CDC — USB Communications Device Class
p: Glossary
x: The standard for a virtual serial port over USB. On the C3 and S3, if "USB CDC On Boot" is not enabled, Serial messages won't come out of the USB cable.

p: Glossary
x: USB built into the chip itself (on the S2, S3, C3, C6, H2 and P4), so it connects straight to a computer without a converter chip like the CP2102.

p: Glossary
x: A standard hardware debugging interface: it lets you pause the program on the chip itself and look at the values of variables.

p: Glossary
x: The USB class for keyboards, mice and gamepads. The S2 and S3 can pretend to be a keyboard.

p: Glossary
x: The ESP32 crash message: the program hit a fatal error (for example, accessing invalid memory) and the chip resets.

p: Glossary
x: The list of addresses of the functions that were running at the moment of a crash. The Exception Decoder turns them into function names and line numbers.

p: Glossary
x: A tool that translates a crash backtrace into the exact line of your code.

p: Glossary
x: A guard timer: if the program gets stuck and doesn't check in on time, it resets the chip.

p: Glossary
x: The program's dynamic memory (used by String, for example). If it keeps shrinking over time, that's a sign of a memory leak.

p: Glossary
x: A tool that records fast digital signals and decodes protocols such as I2C and SPI.

p: Glossary
x: A low-power IPv6 mesh network on 802.15.4 radio and the foundation of the Matter standard. The C6 and H2 support it.

p: Glossary
x: A low-power mesh networking protocol for smart homes, running on 802.15.4 radio. Available on the C6 and H2.

p: Glossary
x: A shared smart-home standard (Apple, Google, Amazon) that runs over Wi-Fi or Thread.

p: Glossary
x: An open, royalty-free processor architecture, used in the ESP32-C3, C6, H2 and P4.

p: Glossary
x: A processor architecture from Cadence, used in the classic ESP32, the S2 and the S3.

p: Glossary
x: A digital audio bus for microphones, digital speakers and audio DACs.

p: Glossary
x: A long-range (several kilometers), low-power, low-speed radio modulation, used with modules such as the SX1276 or SX1262.

p: Glossary
x: Espressif's official, full-featured programming framework. The Arduino ESP32 core is built on top of it.

p: Glossary
x: An electronic switch controlled by the voltage on its gate, drawing almost no control current. Great for loads of several amps and for PWM.

p: Glossary
x: A MOSFET that turns fully on with a logic voltage (3.3 or 5 V). The IRF540N and IRFZ44N are not logic-level; the AO3400 and IRLZ44N are.

p: Glossary
x: A transistor's current gain: how many times larger the collector current can be than the base current (for example, 100 times).

p: Glossary
x: A diode placed across a coil (relay, motor), connected the reverse way, so the voltage spike when the current is switched off doesn't destroy the transistor.

p: Glossary
x: The voltage a coil or motor generates by itself when its current changes or when it spins.

p: Glossary
x: Four switches arranged like the letter H that reverse the direction of current through a motor, so it can spin backward.

p: Glossary
x: A motor that turns by exactly one fixed step for each command, for precise motion (3D printers, CNC machines).

p: Glossary
x: A chip with seven Darlington transistors and built-in diodes; the usual driver for the 28BYJ-48 motor.

p: Glossary
x: A color LED with a tiny built-in chip that gets its own color over a single data wire. You can chain hundreds of them.

p: Glossary
x: A part that carries a signal from one circuit to another using light, with no electrical connection between them.

p: Glossary
x: A relay with no moving parts that switches using semiconductors. It is silent, but lets a little current leak through even when off.

p: Glossary
x: The current a motor draws when it is stuck or just starting up: several times its normal current.

p: Glossary
x: A small program inside the chip that runs at power-up. If GPIO0 is held LOW, it waits to receive a new program.

p: Glossary
x: The white text printed on a board, such as pin labels (D2, GND, 3V3).

p: Glossary
x: The voltage drop across an LED or diode while it conducts: about 2 V for a red LED and about 3 V for blue and white ones.

p: Glossary
x: Reading an input over and over in loop to notice when it changes. Simpler than an interrupt.

p: Glossary
x: A community-maintained PlatformIO platform that supports version 3 of the Arduino ESP32 core.

p: Glossary
x: A pipe with a fixed number of slots that tasks use to pass data to each other safely, as copies, in first-in first-out order.

p: Glossary
x: A lock: only one task at a time can use a shared resource (such as Serial). Every Take must be matched by a Give.

p: Glossary
x: The part of FreeRTOS that decides, based on priority, which task runs at each moment.

p: Glossary
x: Each task's private memory for local variables and function calls. On the ESP32 its size is given in bytes, and making it too small causes crashes.

p: Glossary
x: A bug that appears when two tasks touch the same data at the same time, so the result is occasionally wrong.

p: Glossary
x: Installing a new program on the ESP32 over Wi-Fi, with no USB cable.

p: Glossary
x: How the flash memory is divided into sections such as app0, app1, nvs and spiffs. OTA needs two app sections.

p: Glossary
x: Automatically going back to the previous program version when the new version doesn't confirm that it is working.

p: Glossary
x: A lightweight file system on the ESP32's flash that survives power cuts. Used for web pages, settings and logs.

p: Glossary
x: Spreading writes across the whole flash memory so no single spot wears out early.

p: Glossary
x: HTTP encrypted with TLS. It hides the content and (with a certificate) also verifies the server's identity.

p: Glossary
x: A server's signed ID card. The root CA is the trusted authority whose signature vouches for that card.

p: Glossary
x: Dynamic memory getting chopped into small pieces from constantly creating and deleting Strings. Over time it leads to crashes.

p: Glossary
x: Why the ESP32 last reset (power loss, crash, watchdog, brownout), which you can read with esp_reset_reason().

p: Glossary
x: A URL that triggers an action when you send an HTTP request to it, for example a notification on your phone with ntfy.

p: Glossary
x: The number in a server's reply: 200 means success, 404 means not found, 429 means too many requests, and 500 and above means a server error.

p: Glossary
x: The security layer that encrypts internet traffic and checks the server's identity with a certificate. It is the basis of HTTPS and secure MQTT (port 8883).

p: Glossary
x: A periodic "I'm still here" message between a device and a server, so an idle connection doesn't get dropped.

p: Glossary
x: The unique name of each device on the broker. If two devices use the same client ID, they keep kicking each other off.

p: Glossary
x: The minimum difference needed between a regulator's input and output voltage. For example, the AMS1117 needs about 1 V, so it can't deliver a stable 3.3 V from a 3.7 V battery.

p: Glossary
x: The Wi-Fi radio switches off between the router's beacon signals to save power. This can make ESP-NOW messages get lost; to prevent it, call WiFi.setSleep(false).

p: Glossary
x: Ignoring very small changes (such as a jittery potentiometer reading) so the output doesn't twitch for no reason.

p: Glossary
x: A BLE descriptor that a phone writes to in order to turn automatic updates (notify) on or off.

p: Glossary
x: The separate power pin for the coils on a relay module. Removing the jumper separates the ESP32 side from the coil side.

p: Glossary
x: When your internet provider doesn't give you your own public IP address, which is why devices at home can't be reached directly from outside.

p: Glossary
x: A page that opens automatically after you join a Wi-Fi network. WiFiManager uses one to ask you for your Wi-Fi password.

p: Glossary
x: A tool for measuring voltage, current, resistance and continuity (beep). The most important tool for troubleshooting hardware.

p: Glossary
x: The manufacturer's official document for a part, listing all its technical specs (voltages, pins, limits). The final word in any argument.
